digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate impact model calibration (plan-v3 → plan-v4)
propositions: The divergent_implementation axis fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings despite being the sole hard-override axis never calibrated, and is graded none ~90% of the time within the omitted-scope-site class it exists to describe, causing real plan divergences to score impact 0.0

The G6 finding c4ad-a93e-0613-408f would cause runtime failures (corpus re-embedding on boot, wipe routed to LanceDB drop) but scored impact 0.0 because all seven impact axes were graded none, leaving no axis to fire on the divergent implementation

The divergent_implementation axis must be regraded from ordinal (none/low/medium/high) to a closed Literal set with three kinds (contradicts_reality, omits_required_site, incomplete_enumeration) that floors differently and requires excluded handling in impact_plan's contribution loop

The impact_plan resolution must be restructured to exclude divergent_implementation from the generic _SEV01 contribution map and instead resolve it through a new DIVERGENCE_GRADE01 map, keeping hard-floor semantics for contradicts_reality and omits_required_site while routing incomplete_enumeration below all blocking thresholds

A production-impact floor would destabilize the remediation loop's novelty-driven convergence by lifting an unbounded severity band that cannot be remediated by plan edits, whereas divergence grading lifts a semantically bounded class (misdescription or under-scoping) that terminates remediation when fixed

ADR-0054 must mandate that calibration instruments be confined to corpus replay and dogfooding against existing data, explicitly rejecting high-cost purpose-built LLM evaluation suites or bulk re-review runs, narrowing ADR-0036's A/B clause while preserving version-segmentation and the permissive-rollout invariant
